claims.statement: The pinned default-image fragment asserts JupyterLab is included for codespaces built from that image. For nondefault images it describes adding the Python feature with installJupyterlab true. This conditional installation recipe is unexecuted evidence, not permission to install or proof of an actual image/application; linked moving image/feature repositories and introduction remain separate.

Opening through JupyterLab requires the application installed in the chosen codespace and includes the default-image fragment. This prerequisite is not a universal Jupyter mandate or verified installation; a reviewed child fragment does not certify composed rendering.

Existing-codespace direct links are owner-only in this fragment; other users receive 404. Link construction uses the unique permanent codespace name, not display name, and supports web, web-with-folder, desktop-editor and Jupyter routes. Example names and workspace paths are placeholders, not real targets. A direct editor link is distinct from forwarded-port sharing and not a grant of shared access.

The getting-started fragment routes readers separately to quickstart, repository creation, template creation, reopening and architecture explanation. References do not constitute review of those articles, executed creation or current account eligibility.

Unpublished template-created codespaces not linked to a hosted repository have fixed VM specifications and cannot change machine type. This exception narrows the generic change-machine procedures in DOCS-CODESPACESRETENTION-002 and DOCS-CODESPACESTRANSITION-002/003; retain lifecycle applicability rather than inventing a universally available resizing operation.

Creation-count and concurrent-running limits vary with unspecified factors; at a creation maximum the source describes a message requiring removal of an existing instance before another can be created. No numerical limit is supplied. The message is not authorization to delete or evidence of recoverable custody.

The devcontainer reference points to the external Development Containers specification for available settings/properties. It does not enumerate or certify the whole specification, resolve its version or prove a configuration conforms.
The navigation step opens the user's Codespaces listing. A URL and navigation instruction do not prove authenticated access, inventory completeness or permission to mutate listed instances.
